claims.text: Multiclass set-valued classifiers can guarantee user-defined levels of coverage while minimizing ambiguity.
Oracle set-valued classifiers are obtained from level sets of the conditional probability functions of each class.
Set-valued classification estimators can be built on existing single-label classifiers.
The optimal set-valued classifier can sometimes output the empty set.
Two solutions are provided to prevent the optimal set-valued classifier from outputting the empty set.

evidence.description: We introduce a framework for multiclass set-valued classification, where the classifiers guarantee user-defined levels of coverage or confidence (the probability that the true label is contained in the set) while minimizing the ambiguity (the expected size of the output).
We show that the oracle classifiers are obtained from level sets of the functions that define the conditional probability of each class.
The proposed estimators build on existing single-label classifiers.
The optimal classifier can sometimes output the empty set
we provide two solutions to fix this issue that are suitable for various practical needs.

methodologies.name: Multiclass set-valued classification framework
methodologies.description: A framework for set-valued classification that constructs estimators from existing single-label classifiers to guarantee coverage levels while minimizing set size.

limitations.text: The optimal classifier can sometimes output the empty set.
